runs.text: Short-run cost curves move differently because fixed costs affect AFC and ATC, while variable-input costs affect AVC, ATC, and MC. A below-average marginal observation pulls the average down. Labor is the variable input in the standard short-run model. A fixed-cost increase raises fixed cost per unit and total cost per unit but leaves variable and marginal cost unchanged.

runs.text: Quantity horizontal; cost per unit vertical. Original ATC equals AVC plus 250 divided by Q. Higher fixed cost makes ATC equal AVC plus 500 divided by Q, above original ATC at every positive output. AVC and MC remain unchanged. The ATC-AVC gap declines with Q for either fixed-cost amount.

runs.text: Suppose the firm signs a more expensive lease while output and variable input prices are unchanged. The higher fixed cost raises average fixed cost and therefore shifts ATC upward. AVC and MC remain in the positions shown because neither depends on fixed cost. The production decision at the margin is unchanged.

THE CORE IDEA

HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
A fixed-cost increase raises fixed cost per unit and total cost per unit but leaves variable and marginal cost unchanged.
A technology improvement reduces the variable input needed at every output.
Labor is the variable input in the standard short-run model.
